### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**5** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8dd8192cbfb35dddc4f38f228edc1fb62c909ad3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e5cb39adb776d4c2887b29c46aed9bc1b46eb471` — the merge of head `a6661f57e8538c32b72f476959d3f3d1151b292e` into base `8dd8192cbfb35dddc4f38f228edc1fb62c909ad3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e5cb39adb776d4c2887b29c46aed9bc1b46eb471 && git checkout e5cb39adb776d4c2887b29c46aed9bc1b46eb471
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8dd8192cbfb35dddc4f38f228edc1fb62c909ad3 a6661f57e8538c32b72f476959d3f3d1151b292e && git checkout -B drift-repro 8dd8192cbfb35dddc4f38f228edc1fb62c909ad3 && git merge --no-ff a6661f57e8538c32b72f476959d3f3d1151b292e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8dd8192cbfb35dddc4f38f228edc1fb62c909ad3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## 席位核对

**L1 verdict: REWORK** (one test, no source change) · PR #34592 · card #34554 · first review · read 2026-11-17T03:23Z

Head-sha: `e62453cb2b50e77b7ee5c574be11b9b0e975a25b` (the head named in final-head comment 6937085226)

I read this head on GitHub (`get`, the diff, check-runs), not from the report. The code is right as I read it. One promise this change rests on is not pinned, and the area asked me to check exactly that promise.

**Checklist**
- Shape: draft, base `main`. The body opens with the attribution lines, then `Fixes #34554`. The card (S5 of contract review 6933814641 on #34494) is delivered whole. No other card number sits next to a closing verb.
- Scope: 4 files.
  - `meta-overlay-cache.ts`: `since`, `advance()`, and the new export `readOverlayCacheGenerationSince`.
  - `meta-compile-cache.ts`: the keep-or-retire branch where a new bucket opens, and the header.
  - Its test file.
  - A root changeset, patch for `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`.
  No `content/docs/releases/`. `Clause-②: no` holds: the new export is a package-internal helper, and no wire answer, schema or knob moves.
- Published text, sentence by sentence:
  - Changeset:
    - "every list read moves `registry.revision`, even when it registers what is already there": this is the measured S5 shape, which the new group's non-vacuity assertion reproduces on the double.
    - "opening a bucket retired the `sys_metadata` row cache": the removed lines say so.
    - "3 … against 1 …, and 7 against 3": this matches the ablation's `[3,3,3,3]` against `[3,1,1,1]` and `[7,7,7,7]` against `[7,3,3,3]`.
    - "its first bound ends one bound after they were read, so no answer carries a row more than one bound old": true as code. The bound ends at `since + ttl`, and every held row set was read at or after `since`. The anchor is the generation's start, which is at or before each read, so the sentence errs on the safe side.
    - "When the rows are older than that, opening the bucket retires them, as before": true (the `else` arm).
    - "now costs what it costs with the compile cache off": pinned (`on` equals `off`).
  - Docs: the compile-cache sentences in `concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx` (:315–330) and the `OS_METADATA_COMPILE_CACHE_TTL_MS` row of `deployment/environment-variables.mdx` were re-read. "A peer's write that reaches no epoch is seen at its own bound" and "each confirmation also retires the overlay row cache" are still true, and neither page says that a counter move retires the rows. No page goes stale.
- Gates: 51 check-runs on this head, all `completed`: 35 `success`, 16 `skipped`, 0 failed. Lint & Repo Gates `success`, TypeScript Type Check `success`, Test Core `success`, Check Changeset `success`.

**The rewritten #34494 pin, against ADR-0156 D5 (asked by the area)**

The removed pin is "a counter move retires the row cache: a peer's write the row cache predates is in the new bucket's answer". It encoded the old mechanism: retirement on every counter move. This card retires that mechanism on purpose, so the edit is forced. It is replaced by two pins:
- `:650` "[#34554] a counter move keeps the row sets read within the last bound, and a peer's write is in the answer by the next bound".
- `:668` "a counter move retires the row cache once its rows are more than a bound old …". This is the old assertion at the age the rule now names. It also asserts `mark.calls === 0`, which proves the retirement and not a confirmation served the write.

Each of the four promises at this head:
1. No change, no recompile: carried by `:413` ("nothing moved: … no recompile") and the D7 control `:342`, both unchanged. This PR does not change what opens a bucket.
2. A change always recompiles: carried by D7 `:296`–`:329`, unchanged. A counter move still opens a bucket with no entries. The keep branch keeps rows, never compiled answers.
3. A source the confirmation cannot observe is recompiled at its bound: carried by `:697`, unchanged. `confirm()` is untouched.
4. No row in an answer is more than one bound old: **only partly pinned. This is R1.**

**R1 (REWORK) · `meta-compile-cache.test.ts`: pin the first bound's END, `since + ttl`, not only its two sides.**

In `:650` the clock is frozen at `1_000_000` from the first read through the counter move. At that moment `since` equals `now`, so `confirmedUntil = since + ttlMs` and `confirmedUntil = now + ttlMs` give the same value. `:668` takes the `else` arm, and the alternation group runs on the real clock within milliseconds. So this mutation of the keep arm survives all 39 cases:

```ts
if (since !== undefined && since + ttlMs > now) {
    confirmedUntil = now + ttlMs;   // mutant: a kept row can now be served almost two bounds old
}
```

The mutant breaks promise 4. With rows read at T and a counter move at T + 0.9 bound, it serves them until T + 1.9 bounds. This is the one line that turns "keep the rows" from a staleness hole into the bounded rule the changeset states, and the ablation in the body (keep branch off) does not reach it.

The fix is one more case in the same describe, with the same harness and `atBound()`:
- warm the row cache (`Widget`) at T;
- move the clock part of a bound (for example `+20_000`);
- store the peer's `Gadget` and move `registry.revision`;
- assert `Widget` is still served with no row read;
- move the clock to `T + 30_001` (that is, less than one bound after the counter move) and assert `Gadget`.

Then run the ablation above once and record it red. No source change, no changeset change. L2 stays not owed after it.

**Spot checks (mine)**
1. Every place the generation moves goes through `advance()`: the middleware `finally`, the non-`write` epoch subscription, and `retireMetaOverlayCache`. `since` starts at the state's creation. No place moves `gen` without moving `since`.
2. Engines this cache does not cover give `since === undefined`, so the `else` arm runs, `retireMetaOverlayCache` returns `undefined`, and the stamp is unchanged, exactly as on `main`.
3. A local `sys_metadata` write or a bridged peer write moves the generation (the old row sets are refused), sets `since` to now, and changes the stamp. The bucket it opens then keeps an emptied row cache. Writes are not delayed: the "a write is seen at once" pins (`:277`) are unchanged.

**L2 owed: no.** None of the four contract faces is touched: `Clause-②: no`, no narrowing, no `packages/spec/src/**` path, no governed rule text. The opus L2 seat read it the same way.

**Landing tier**: `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34592` reports NOT governed, +156/−20 = 176 lines ≤ 3000. After R1, the area sends the new head to L1-c as a delta. It is then an ordinary queue landing by the area.

**L1 verdict: ACCEPT** · PR #34592 · card #34554 · delta over my REWORK 6937141164 (at `e62453cb`) · read 2026-11-17T03:52Z

Head-sha: `a6661f57e8538c32b72f476959d3f3d1151b292e`

Read from GitHub and the commit at this head, not from the report. Delta: one commit, `a6661f57`, with one file, `meta-compile-cache.test.ts` (+18). No source change and no changeset change. Everything my first read accepted stands as read.

**R1: closed.** The new case at `:668` is "the bucket a counter move opens ends its first bound one bound after the kept rows were read, not one bound after the move". This is how its clock separates the two possible end times:
- It reads at T = `1_000_000`, warming the row cache.
- It moves to T + 20 s, stores the peer's `Gadget`, and moves `registry.revision`.
- It asserts that `Widget` is served with no `find` of the item's rows (kept).
- It sets the clock to T + 30 001 ms, one bound after the rows were read and less than one bound after the move, and asserts `Gadget`.
At that point `since + ttl` = T + 30 000 and `now + ttl` = T + 50 000, so the case tells the two apart. The mutant I named (`confirmedUntil = now + ttlMs` in the keep arm) would still serve `Widget` there. The area records it as 1 of 40 red (`expected 'Widget' to be 'Gadget'`) and 40 of 40 green once restored, in rework comment 6937188352. Promise 4 of ADR-0156 D5 (no row in an answer more than one bound old) is now pinned at its edge, beside `:650` and `:686`.
